criteria.description: The teal outlined triangle keeps its horizontal base endpoints fixed while the gold altitude joins the apex to its perpendicular foot on that base; the ivory right-angle marker is derived from the same foot and stays inside the triangle.

Across the two-second sequence the apex makes a small, smooth horizontal excursion and return, with constant apex height; the altitude stays vertical and attached, and the right-angle marker follows its foot without lag or detachment.
The complete construction is identifiable at the start, the lateral change is readable through the middle, and the geometry settles into a final hold before the two-second endpoint.

Primary geometry and all geometric motion come from a newly generated 48-frame, 24-fps Manim resource, not the earlier single-frame PNG; HTML carries the resource using its embedded manifest and prepareManimMethodFrames(rootElement,manifest,{placementStartFrame:0}).

At the 1280 by 720 viewport, the carrier synchronously exposes window.__animationExperiment with ready:layer.ready and seek(seconds), awaits readiness before initializing seek(0), and produces identical frames for equal absolute times during forward, reverse, repeated, zero and fresh-load seeks.
The composition preserves a warm ivory background, teal fill, dark outline, gold altitude and ivory corner marker, with no text, extra imagery, narration or sound effects.

---
name: shared-construction-motion
description: Plan constrained geometric motion with dependent annotations and transport actual Manim frames through an absolute-time HTML carrier.
---

# When to apply

Use for educational geometry in which one independent change must preserve visible relationships among a shape, measurement line and annotation. Choose Manim resource authoring when the task requires actual Manim geometry; use HTML only to place its real generated frames. This is a draft method, not evidence of a successful render.

# Decide what moves and what must remain true

Identify the subject, independent degrees of freedom, fixed anchors and dependent objects before selecting easing. State the invariant in geometry terms: perpendicularity, shared endpoints, equal distances or another meaningful relation. Derive dependent geometry from the same current construction points instead of independently tweening each object. Reveal a relation only when the explanation calls for its introduction; if the task begins with a complete annotated construction, preserve that complete starting state.

For an altitude onto a base with endpoints A and C, compute v=C-A and the projection D=A+dot(B-A,v)/dot(v,v)*v. Reject a zero-length base. This handles sloped bases as well as horizontal ones. Construct the altitude from B to D. Build the right-angle marker in the local base and perpendicular basis, choosing the side that fits inside the subject. A horizontal base permits the simpler foot (B.x,A.y), but that formula must not be generalized to a rotated base. Keep fixed anchors fixed and update the polygon, dependent segment and marker from the same absolute state.

# Shape the expression

Choose a small displacement that makes the relationship readable without changing the intended class of construction. Inspect the proposed full motion envelope analytically for degenerate shapes, exterior feet and marker clearance. A marker may need a smaller size or a different interior side for changed content. Use an initial orientation hold, a purposeful change and a final reading hold. Allocate timing to the semantic event rather than applying a uniform entrance to every object. A return movement is appropriate when the goal is to demonstrate persistence under perturbation; a one-way change may better explain a new state. Do not add a return merely because this sample has one.

In native Manim, animate the independent parameter and recompute dependent objects together during resource production. Avoid separate endpoint animations whose easing can disagree. Preserve the requested duration, fps, transparency and frame inventory. Let the trusted producer perform rendering; never claim that authored Python alone demonstrates working motion.

# Transport the actual result

Require a newly generated resource manifest for the current animation. Do not recycle a static origin image, guess resource identities or fabricate hashes. Include only dependencies admitted by the carrier task. HTML may provide background and uniform placement; it must not redraw or fake the required Manim subject. Match aspect ratio and determine scale from resource and viewport dimensions. If raster enlargement is required, treat edge quality as unresolved until rendered.

Create the real resource layer through prepareManimMethodFrames(rootElement,manifest,{placementStartFrame:0}). Immediately expose window.__animationExperiment with ready:layer.ready and an absolute seek(seconds) method. Await layer.ready before the initial seek(0), so decoding precedes frame selection. Derive each requested resource frame directly from seconds and fps with an explicit interval policy; clamp out-of-range times and the inclusive scene endpoint to a valid frame. Forward that frame to layer.seekFrame. Never advance from prior frame state, read wall-clock time, start timers or add autonomous playback. Reverse, repeated and fresh-load seeks must select the same frame for the same absolute time. This seconds interface belongs to the laboratory host; adapt to a different host's documented frame contract explicitly.

# Adaptation decisions

For changed geometry, recompute projection and annotation basis instead of retaining screen offsets. For changed duration, rebalance observation holds and motion time while keeping all production frames inside the requested interval. For changed viewport, preserve geometry aspect ratio and reassess stroke visibility after transport. For changed teaching goals, select the invariant and degrees of freedom anew; do not reuse a triangle composition for unrelated structures. Keep sounds absent when requested; otherwise describe purposeful host sound events separately from scene code.

# Failure modes and counterexamples

A marker tweened independently can drift even when its final position is correct. A pre-rendered single frame cannot demonstrate a changing construction. Updating only the altitude while leaving the filled shape unchanged breaks endpoint attachment. Reusing a horizontal projection for a sloped base produces a false right angle. A large apex excursion can send the foot outside the base or crowd the marker against an edge. Decoding after initialization can leave a blank first capture. Mapping the inclusive endpoint to frame_count selects a nonexistent frame. Browser scaling can soften an otherwise precise construction. These are risks and geometric counterexamples, not claims of observed failures in this task.

# Evidence and handoff

Keep planning, source authoring, producer output, actual render, sampled-frame assessment and explicit developer acceptance distinct. Require the producer's real frame inventory and manifest before writing the carrier. Later evaluate geometry at extrema and holds, then assess actual motion and seek behavior through the trusted host. Still images alone do not establish timing continuity, audio or complete playback. Preserve failures and uncertainty in subsequent records. Do not infer acceptance, transfer or publication from a successful file write.
